## Context

**As** the RumaQ maintainer
**Given** the typed API client is generated by `openapi-typescript` and consumed by `openapi-fetch` — two releases a year each, no TypeScript 7 support in any published version ([#2841](https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript/issues/2841), PRs #2867/#2872 open since September)
**When** the generator and client move to `hey-api/openapi-ts`
**Then** the hand-written client contract is unchanged, the generator is actively maintained (524 releases in 12 months), and the JS compiler stays confined to `tools/codegen`

## Summary

Swaps the frontend's typed API client stack from `openapi-typescript` + `openapi-fetch` to `@hey-api/openapi-ts`. The generated client is emitted into `frontend/src/lib/api-client/` (committed, lint/fmt-ignored, drift-checked in CI). `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` keeps its exported surface — same ~96 functions, same `ApiError`, `Retry-After` parsing and throwing semantics — and now calls generated SDK functions instead of `client.GET('/api/…')`. Document uploads now pass multipart fields as a plain object, because the generated client serialises FormData from own enumerable entries and a pre-built `FormData` has none (that would have uploaded an empty body).

## Architecture

- `tools/codegen` runs `@hey-api/openapi-ts@0.99.0` via `openapi-ts.config.ts`, and still pins `typescript@5.9.3`: hey-api, like the old generator, builds its output through the JS compiler API (`ts.factory`, `ts.SyntaxKind`) and resolves the app's compiler — under TS 7 it dies on `ts.SyntaxKind.AnyKeyword` regardless of its permissive peer range. The pin is what lets the root tree stay on TypeScript 7.
- Generated output is committed so the existing CI drift check fails when backend routes change: `frontend/openapi.json` + `frontend/src/lib/api-client/**`.
- `@hey-api/client-fetch@0.13.1` (zero dependencies) replaces `openapi-fetch` as the runtime client; `credentials: 'include'` is applied once via `client.setConfig`.

## Backend

None. The OpenAPI spec and route surface are untouched; the codegen drift check still guards them.

## Frontend

- `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`: 93 call sites rewritten to the generated SDK; every exported function keeps its name and signature, so all query modules (`frontend/src/lib/queries/*`) are untouched.
- Multipart uploads (`createDocument`, `addDocumentFile`) now pass `{ name, file, label, memberId }` instead of a raw `FormData`; two new tests pin the shape and explain the empty-body trap.
- `api.test.js` / `queries/me.test.js` mock the generated client boundary; body-carrying assertions use `objectContaining` because the generated SDK attaches its own `Content-Type`.
- Proof: `./scripts/test.sh unit frontend` → **828 passed** (66 files); build 245.1 KB gzipped against the 250 KB budget.

## Security Review

- No new runtime surface: same `fetch`, same origin, `credentials: 'include'`, cookie session and CSRF behaviour unchanged.
- Dependency delta: `openapi-typescript` (build) and `openapi-fetch` (runtime) removed; `@hey-api/openapi-ts@0.99.0` (build) and `@hey-api/client-fetch@0.13.1` (runtime, no dependencies, MIT) added. `bun audit` clean in CI.
- The generated client is committed and treated as generated code: excluded from lint, but its types are type-checked through `api.ts`, which is linted.
- The multipart change removes a silent-failure path (an empty upload) rather than adding exposure.

## Performance Review

- Total bundle **245.1 KB gzipped** (was 244.4 KB, +0.7 KB) — inside the 250 KB budget.
- Codegen is ~0.4 s; generated SDK functions are ordinary per-operation functions, so route-level code splitting is unchanged.
- Generated footprint: 4 committed files (~5.4k lines) replace one 6,989-line `.d.ts` — net −1.4k lines in the tree.

- [x] `./scripts/github/ci.sh` passes locally (style/typecheck under TS 7, docs, codegen drift, frontend + backend tests, audit, build, bundle budget)
- [x] Regeneration is deterministic — a second `api:codegen` produces no diff
- [x] Frontend tests: 828 passed, including the two new multipart tests
- [x] `vp check` clean with the generated client in the tree
- [x] Bundle within budget

## Documentation

- [x] `docs/ONBOARDING.md` — `tools/codegen/` row names hey-api and the compiler pin
- [x] `vite.config.ts` — `api:codegen` comment explains why the generator keeps its own compiler and how drift is caught
- [x] `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` header points at `api-client/` as the generated contract

## Limitations & Warnings

- **Stacked on #569**: the base branch is `chore/typescript-7` (this PR needs the `tools/codegen` workspace #569 introduced). Do not merge before #569; GitHub retargets this PR to `main` automatically once #569 merges.
- **Human-review gate: new dependencies.** One build-time and one runtime package from a new vendor; both exact-pinned.
- The `tools/codegen` TypeScript 5.9.3 pin does **not** go away with this migration — hey-api needs the JS compiler API too.
- hey-api is still `0.x` (0.99.0): a minor bump may carry breaking changes; the dependency is exact-pinned for that reason.
- Upstream `openapi-typescript` issues #2841/#2867/#2872 remain open; they no longer block RumaQ.
